Reigning holder Achraf Hakimi, fellow Moroccans Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari, alongside Senegalese duo Sadio Mané and Pape Gueye, made the final list for the continent’s most prestigious individual football honour.
The shortlist, announced by CAF on Tuesday, was trimmed from an initial list of 10 nominees following their performances for club and country during the year under review.
The omission of Osimhen and Salah is a major talking point, with the two forwards among Africa’s most prominent footballers in recent years.
The final five nominees reflect the impressive campaigns of Morocco and Senegal, with the latter winning the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025, while the Atlas Lions reached the final of the continental competition and the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Hakimi, who plays for Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award after another impressive season in which he helped the French giants defend their UEFA Champions League title and retain the Ligue 1 crown.
The Morocco captain also played a leading role in his country’s performances at the AFCON and World Cup.
Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is chasing a third crown after leading Senegal to their second continental title. The Al-Nassr forward was named Player of the Tournament at the AFCON in Morocco.
Diaz earned his nomination after winning the Golden Boot at the tournament with five goals, including strikes in five consecutive matches, as Morocco finished runners-up.
The Real Madrid attacking midfielder also featured prominently in Morocco’s World Cup campaign.
Senegal midfielder Gueye made the shortlist after scoring the decisive extra-time goal in the 1-0 victory over Morocco in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances also earned him a place in the tournament’s Best XI.
Saibari completes the list after playing an influential role in Morocco’s run to the AFCON final and their subsequent World Cup campaign. The midfielder also strengthened his profile with impressive performances at club level.
The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards 2026 ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos.
The ceremony, which will begin at 7pm Nigerian time, marks the return of the CAF Awards to Nigeria’s commercial capital for the first time since 2014.
The CAF Men’s Player of the Year award recognises the African footballer whose performances and achievements for club and country stand out during the period under consideration.
